subject.title: fix(backup): sweep stale temp artifacts before creating new backup

question: After the matcher is repaired, should OpenClaw accept a startup sweep that deletes OpenClaw-owned backup temp artifacts older than one hour, or require a different recovery/debugging policy?
rationale: The patch changes the lifecycle of operator-visible partial backup artifacts; automated review can check scoping and owner guards, but only maintainers can decide whether those stale artifacts are disposable crash leftovers.

options.title: Accept guarded sweep
options.body: Land after the matcher, rebase, tests, and proof are fixed, treating owner-marked one-hour stale backup artifacts as disposable crash leftovers.

options.title: Require recovery surface
options.body: Ask for a visible list, dry-run, or recovery/debug workflow before startup deletion removes stale backup artifacts automatically.

options.title: Do not delete on startup
options.body: Pause or close this direction if stale partial backups must remain for manual operator inspection instead of self-healing on the next run.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded sweep
recommendation.body: Land after the matcher, rebase, tests, and proof are fixed, treating owner-marked one-hour stale backup artifacts as disposable crash leftovers.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to both the original backup CLI merge and the extraction of backup creation into the current infra surface.
